title: A Holiday Cleaning Schedule, Week by Week (So December Isn't One Giant Panic Clean)
description: A gentle week-by-week holiday cleaning schedule for busy brains. Small 15-minute jobs from early November to the big day, so nothing piles up at the end.
intro:
Every year we tell ourselves we'll get the house ready early. Then it's December 22nd, family arrives in two days, and we're scrubbing the oven at midnight while wrapping gifts with the other hand.

That last-minute scramble isn't a character flaw. Our brains run on urgency, and "the holidays" feel far away until they suddenly don't. So let's borrow a little urgency now, in small pieces.

This schedule splits holiday cleaning into one focus per week, with jobs that take 15 minutes or less. Miss a week? Skip it and pick up with the current one. The goal is a home that's ready enough, not perfect.

sections.heading: Before you start: pick your 'guest path'
sections.body:
Guests don't see your whole house. They see the front door, the living room, the kitchen, the guest bathroom and maybe a spare bed. That's your guest path.

Write those spots on a sticky note and put it on the fridge. Every week below, focus on the guest path first. Closets, the garage and your bedroom can wait until January.

sections.heading: Week 1 (early November): clear the surfaces
sections.body:
Flat surfaces collect the most stuff, and clear surfaces make a room look clean even when it isn't.

- **Day 1:** Kitchen counters. Put away anything that doesn't get used daily.
- **Day 2:** Coffee table and side tables.
- **Day 3:** Entry table or the spot where mail lands.
- **Day 4:** Dining table, so you can eat at it again.

Use a "later" box for things you can't decide on. Tape it shut, write the date on it and stash it in a closet. You can sort it after the holidays.

sections.heading: Week 2: the fridge and pantry
sections.body:
Holiday cooking needs space, and that space is currently full of mystery leftovers.

- Toss anything expired or unidentifiable from the fridge. Set a 10-minute timer.
- Wipe one fridge shelf while it's empty.
- Pull expired spices and baking supplies from the pantry.
- Write a short list of what you'll need for holiday cooking and baking.

This also makes Thanksgiving leftovers far less stressful.

sections.heading: Week 3: the guest bathroom
sections.body:
This is the room guests will be alone in, so it's the one we tend to worry about most.

- Clear the counter down to soap, a hand towel and one candle or plant.
- Wipe the mirror and faucet. Two minutes.
- Put a new roll of toilet paper on the holder and two more where guests can see them.
- Empty the trash and add a spare liner under the bag.

The next week, all it needs is a quick wipe.

sections.heading: Week 4: floors and entryway
sections.body:
Winter boots bring in a lot of mess. Get the entry ready before the crowd does.

- Add a boot tray and a sturdy doormat inside the door.
- Clear the floor of the entry so coats and bags have somewhere to go.
- Vacuum or sweep the guest path. One room per day is fine.
- Set up a spot for guests' coats: a few hooks or a cleared section of the closet.

sections.heading: Week 5: beds, towels and the spare room
sections.body:
- Wash guest sheets and put them right back on the bed, so they're ready.
- Set out two towels per guest on the bed or a chair.
- Clear one drawer or a corner for guest suitcases.
- Add a phone charger and a small lamp by the guest bed.

No spare room? Put sheets, a pillow and a blanket in one labeled bag near the couch.

sections.heading: Week 6: decorate, then do a 'last look' pass
sections.body: Decorating goes faster on clean surfaces, which is why it comes last. Once decorations are up, walk the guest path with a laundry basket and grab anything that doesn't belong. Ten minutes, done.

sections.heading: The day before guests arrive
sections.body:
Keep this list short on purpose:

- Empty the dishwasher so it's ready for the next load.
- Quick wipe of the guest bathroom sink and toilet.
- Take out kitchen and bathroom trash.
- Run the laundry basket sweep one more time.

Then stop. Seriously. The house is ready enough, and the people coming over are there to see you, not your baseboards.

sections.heading: If you're starting late
sections.body: Got two weeks instead of six? Do Week 1 (surfaces) and Week 3 (bathroom) only. Those two give you the biggest visible change for the least time. Everything else is a bonus.

outro:
Holiday cleaning feels huge because we picture it all at once. Split into tiny weekly jobs, it's a few minutes a day, and December gets to be about the fun stuff.

If you want this as a checklist you can stick on the fridge, the *Tidy Brain Printable Pack* has room-by-room cleaning lists ready to print.
